rule: Several rectangular one-pixel frames, each in its own colour, are split into compartments by internal walls. Later frames cover earlier ones where straight walls cross at right angles. One noise colour, the colour with the most 8-connected pieces, is scattered over the grid and hides some wall cells. A covered run on a frame line is read as wall if it is 1 cell long, or if it is 2-3 cells long and the wall visibly continues past one end; this reading is repeated until stable. Count each frame's closed compartments. Output one row per frame, sorted by count in ascending order, with the lower-layer frame first on a tie. Each row holds count cells of the frame colour, padded with the noise colour to the maximum count.
scope: Constructive overlapping rectangular frames with banded compartments, independent paint order, scattered/occluding noise, iterative 1-to-3-cell wall reconstruction and visible overlap tie-breaking; 3..5 frames on native 14..30 grids.

authored_scope: Random scenes have 3-5 frames with counts 1..6, and at most one tied pair, which is always visibly layered. Grid sides are 14..30. This synthetic range covers the fixture sizes. The per-side lower bound is 14, 16 or 18 for 3, 4 or 5 frames, and when both sides are given their sum must be at least twice that bound. Frames are outlines with full dividers along one axis plus partial walls within each band, giving banded rectangular compartments. Frames may nest, and they cross perpendicularly. Noise does five things: it hides single cells and corners; it builds 2-3 cell gaps; it builds multi-pass gap chains; it creates unbridgeable false walls; and it is scattered over the background. Explicit latent scenes (frames, noise) reproduce the fixtures. They are rejected when the noise colour does not dominate, when a frame colour is fully hidden, when a tie is not visibly layered, or when the output would be wider than 30. Not supported: L-shaped compartments, diagonal or non-rectangular frames, more than 5 random frames, counts above 6 in random mode, and readability or crossing-geometry checks for explicit scenes.
authored_constraints: Frame colours are distinct, nonzero and differ from the noise colour.
Frame overlaps occur only at perpendicular crossings of two straight walls.

On the final grid, every frame's visible evidence, read with the iterative occlusion convention, reconstructs exactly its latent walls, except for hidden outer corners. Every side of every frame keeps a visible cell.
On the final random grid, the noise colour has at least 2 more 8-connected pieces than any frame colour. Explicit scenes need a strict majority.
At most one pair of frames shares a count in random scenes. For that pair, the later frame visibly passes over the earlier one and never the reverse.
Output width equals the maximum count, which is at most 6 in random scenes and at most 30 in explicit scenes. The number of rows equals the number of frames.
All controls must be plain integers. Booleans and floats are rejected.
Every rejection loop is bounded: at most 300 scene attempts and bounded inner retries.
